plain_english: The fruit may be clear and primary, or it may be the final result; it may belong to the main element or to an auxiliary; and it may appear in its opposite, in another side, or in some other opposing condition.
sanskrit_cite:
yādṛk phalaṃ sphutaṃ mukhyaṃ paryantaphalam aṅgi vā /
tadaṅgaṃ vā tadvipakṣe parapakṣe paraṃ ca vā // [AgMsv_2.282]

plain_english: Even one who becomes a vessel for manifesting aspects of various opposites is affected by having a suitable body and by sharing in the proper preparatory conditioning.
sanskrit_cite:
api tattadvipakṣāṃśasamudbhāvanabhājanam /
tathocitaśarīrādes tathā saṃskārabhāginaḥ // [AgMsv_2.283]

plain_english: Such a sequence of qualification is declared for both teacher and student, just as in the case of someone who undertakes the procedure of the death-destroying elixir.
sanskrit_cite:
guroḥ śiṣyasya cāpy uktas tādṛśo 'dhikriyākramaḥ /
tathā ca mṛtyuvidhvaṃsirasāyanavidhiṃ śritaḥ // [AgMsv_2.284]

plain_english: First, for the sake of gaining the proper preparation, one uses decoction, emesis, and purgation; and the alteration brought about by initiation should not occur later during the ritual procedure.
sanskrit_cite:
pūrvaṃ saṃskāralābhāya kvāthavāntivirecanaiḥ /
dīkṣayā yā ca vikṛtiḥ nottaratra kriyāvidhau // [AgMsv_2.285]

plain_english: Therefore the restriction of qualification arises from factors such as one's body and knowledge; for this reason Vaishnavas and others, who depend on the discipline of bound souls, are spoken of as limited in that way.
sanskrit_cite:
tenādhikāriniyamas taddehavidaśādijaḥ /
tenocyate vaiṣṇavādyāḥ paśuśāsanasaṃśritāḥ // [AgMsv_2.286]

plain_english: They are not qualified in the Shaiva scripture; Shaivas are not qualified in the left sphere; those are not qualified in the right; and those are not qualified in the Kula doctrine or in the Trika.
sanskrit_cite:
na śaive 'dhikṛtās tantre na śaivā vāmagocare /
te 'pi no dakṣiṇe te 'pi na syuḥ kulamate trike // [AgMsv_2.287]

plain_english: It is said in the revered Bhairava Kula that the teacher fit for the rite of the five initiations is one who has transcended the lower streams or who is grounded in the Trika scripture.
sanskrit_cite:
uktaṃ śrībhairavakule pañcadīkṣākriyocitaḥ /
gurur ullaṅghitādhastyasrotā vā trikaśāstragaḥ // [AgMsv_2.288]

plain_english: Thus there is a single qualification insofar as all rely on the self-principle, yet qualification becomes differentiated because of differences in preparation.
sanskrit_cite:
ittham ekādhikāritvam ātmatattvasamāśrayāt /
saṃskārāśraya .... bhedād bhinnādhikāritā // [AgMsv_2.289]

plain_english: Therefore it is said in the Svacchanda Tantra that in every scripture Shiva is the fruit, because all arise from Shiva and all have Shiva's abode as their fruit.
sanskrit_cite:
svacchandatantre tenoktaṃ sarvaśāstre śivaḥ phalam /
yataḥ śivodbhavāḥ sarve śivadhāmaphalā iti // [AgMsv_2.290]

plain_english: And there again it is declared, in the discussion of the higher principles: what is not known by the Samkhyas, not by the great yogins, and not, O beloved, by the Pancharatrikas.
sanskrit_cite:
tatraiva ca punaḥ proktam ūrdhvatattvavivecane /
yan na sāṃkhyair na yogīndrair na priye pāñcarātrikaiḥ // [AgMsv_2.291]

plain_english: Thus, as many as three hundred and sixty-three disputants are challenged, for they discriminate only within that limited measure.
sanskrit_cite:
iyādi yāvad ākṣiptaṃ vādināṃ tu śatatrayam /
triṣaṣṭyā cādhikaṃ te hi tāvanmātravivecakāḥ // [AgMsv_2.292]

plain_english: How could they be knowers whose very nature is knowledge of the unlimited Shiva principle? Now suppose they posit the presence of Shiva even in that mere partial portion.
sanskrit_cite:
kathaṃ syur aparicchinnaśivatattvavidātmakāḥ /
atha tatrāṃśamātre 'pi śivasadbhāvam eva te // [AgMsv_2.293]

plain_english: If they were to superimpose that, it would not be clearly coherent; for in a sentence like 'Devadatta,' the reference is to a complete form in every respect.
sanskrit_cite:
āropayeyus tat tāvan naiva suspaṣṭasaṃgati /
devadattādivākye hi sarvataḥ pūrṇavigrahe // [AgMsv_2.294]

plain_english: How could someone who hears only the word 'Devadatta' superimpose upon that limited word the meaning of entire previous sentences?
sanskrit_cite:
devadattapadaśrotā tāvanmātrapade katham /
samagrapūrvavākyānāṃ samāropaṃ kariṣyati // [AgMsv_2.295]

plain_english: And how could he understand so much meaning from the sentence? If one says, 'just from that,' then he is not merely a hearer of a word, nor—
sanskrit_cite:
kathaṃ cādhigamas tasya tāvato 'rthasya vākyataḥ /
tasmād eveti cet tarhi na padaśrotṛtā na ca // [AgMsv_2.296]

plain_english: —is that the meaning of only that much. Thus, in the present domain, understanding must come through knowledge of the entire meaning of the Shaiva scripture in its complete form.
sanskrit_cite:
tāvanmātrasya so 'sty artha itthaṃ prakṛtigocare /
samagraśivaśāstrārthajñaptyā saṃpūrṇarūpayā // [AgMsv_2.297]

plain_english: If one were to construe Yoga, Samkhya, Arhata, Nyaya, Pancharatra, Veda, and Smriti as complete through the Shiva principle—
sanskrit_cite:
yogasāṃkhyārhatanyāyapāñcarātraśrutismṛtīḥ /
yady eva śivatattvena saṃpūrṇaṃ parikalpayet // [AgMsv_2.298]

plain_english: Let that be granted to that extent; but the full expansion is not there. It has been examined that knowledge of the Shiva principle must be preceded by the proper preparation.
sanskrit_cite:
tāvad astu na tu sphāras tāvāṃs tatreti carcitam /
jñaptiś ca śivatattvasya tatsaṃskārapuraḥsarā // [AgMsv_2.299]

plain_english: Otherwise there would be a transgression for both teacher and student; but if the proper preparation is received, then the meaning of the scripture may indeed be of that kind.
sanskrit_cite:
anyathā pratyavāyaḥ syād upadeṣṭrupadeśyayoḥ /
tatsaṃskāragrahaś cet syāt kāmaṃ śāstrārtha īdṛśaḥ // [AgMsv_2.300]

plain_english: But even after receiving higher and higher preparation, he does not cease to be Vaishnava, Samkhya, or Vedic in identity; he still continues to practice accordingly.
sanskrit_cite:
na tu vaiṣṇavatā tasya sāṃkhyatā śrautatāpi vā /
anyasaṃskāram ūrdhvordhaṃ gṛhītvāpy anutiṣṭhati // [AgMsv_2.301]

plain_english: Then, if he remains Vaishnava and so on, his transgression is even greater. But surely, in this nondual state, what is this primary conceptual restriction?
sanskrit_cite:
vaiṣṇavādy eva tarhy asya pratyavāyo mahattaraḥ /
nanv advayapade 'muṣmin keyaṃ mukhyā prakalpanā // [AgMsv_2.302]

plain_english: What are you saying? You yourself, whose conduct is struck by duality, have resorted to this very supreme duality.
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ brūṣe svayam eva tvaṃ bhedopahatavṛttikaḥ /
etad eva paraṃ dvaitaṃ bhavān eva saṃśritaḥ // [AgMsv_2.303]

plain_english: When you say, 'Being a Vaishnava, why am I not qualified in the Shaiva domain?' you yourself are deluded by duality; and in duality, restriction applies by force.
sanskrit_cite:
yad ahaṃ vaiṣṇavo bhūṣṇuḥ śaive kiṃ nādhikāravān /
tat svayaṃ bhedamūḍhas tvaṃ bhede ca niyater balāt // [AgMsv_2.304]

plain_english: Therefore, by those rules, transgression would arise; this has been established. Moreover, a deity is worshiped through identification, and so—
sanskrit_cite:
tatas taiḥ pratyavāyaḥ syād yoga ity upapāditam /
kiṃ ca tādātmyayogena devatā pūjyate tataḥ // [AgMsv_2.305]

plain_english: If someone has become identified with Vishnu, how could that person worship Rudra? The Gita says that whoever has faith in a particular deity is, in effect, that very deity.
sanskrit_cite:
viṣṇutādātmyam āpannaḥ kathaṃ rudraṃ prapūjayet /
gītāsu ca tato gītaṃ yo yac chraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ // [AgMsv_2.306]

plain_english: Practices of contemplating identity with a deity, along with mantras, give their own results. Therefore, for someone whose self has been shaped by that contemplation and who desires a particular fruit, they bring success.
sanskrit_cite:
tādātmyabhāvanā yogāḥ phalaṃ mantrāḥ sva }} /
dadyus tadbhāvitātmātaḥ phalakāmasya siddhidaḥ // [AgMsv_2.307]

plain_english: For someone who desires liberation, even one who seeks liberation through a particular scripture, it is clear that being overcome by dwelling on its faults makes a person capable only within that limited application.
sanskrit_cite:
mokṣakāmasya tac chāstramokṣalipsor api sphuṭam /
taddoṣabhāvanākrāntaḥ kṣamas tāvati yojane // [AgMsv_2.308]

plain_english: This indeed is the primary method: whoever is established in any domain and has permanently attained identity with it is authorized there.
sanskrit_cite:
mukhyas tāvad ayaṃ kalpo yo yatraiva pratiṣṭhitaḥ /
nityaṃ tādātmyam āpannaḥ sa tatrādhikṛtas tv iti // [AgMsv_2.309]

plain_english: For that very reason it is said that knowledge should be received from him, since he has attained identity through the ordered method of contemplating that.
sanskrit_cite:
ata eva tato grāhyaṃ jñānam ity abhidhīyate /
sa hi tādātmyam āpannas tadbhāvanavidhikramāt // [AgMsv_2.310]

plain_english: But when a student is only then receiving the scripture in its proper sequence, how could he at first connect by his own understanding what is coherently taught in it?
sanskrit_cite:
śiṣyas tadaiva śāstraṃ tu gṛhṇan pūrvāparakramāt /
kathaṃ svabuddhyā saṃdhattāṃ tāvad yat tena saṃhitam // [AgMsv_2.311]

plain_english: But whoever strives to join the teaching together by himself is directly the supreme lord; what could a teacher do for him? He is called the teacher of others.
sanskrit_cite:
yas tu saṃdhātum īheta sa sākṣāt parameśvaraḥ /
tasya kiṃ vā guruḥ kuryāt so 'nyeṣāṃ gurur ucyate // [AgMsv_2.312]

plain_english: For people think that knowledge does not come from anyone other than those who know; therefore one who has attained identity with that is designated a teacher.
sanskrit_cite:
nānyato vedavidbhyaś cetyata eva hi manvate /
tasmāt tādātmyam āpanno gurur ity abhidhīyate // [AgMsv_2.313]

plain_english: And he is so only to that extent and in that domain, not otherwise. But surely, does the meaning of Vaishnava scripture, at the time of contemplating Shiva, become affected?
sanskrit_cite:
sa ca yāvati yatraiva tatra tāvati nānyathā /
nanu vaiṣṇavaśāstrārthas tatkālaṃ śivabhāvanāt // [AgMsv_2.314]

plain_english: If someone says that such identity destroys teacherhood, the person of full understanding replies that this is mere prattle; for in the dramas of Rama and Ravana, these are not actors' roles in that fixed sense.
sanskrit_cite:
tādātmyaṃ gurutāṃ hanti pūrṇadhīḥ pralapaty ayam /
rāmarāvaṇanāṭyeṣu nahy etā naṭabhūmikāḥ // [AgMsv_2.315]

plain_english: Otherness is assumed by changing costume and the like; so too a Vaishnava reflects, 'I am indeed Vishnu' or 'I am his servant.'
sanskrit_cite:
nepathyādiparāvṛttyā yenānyatvaṃ prapadyate /
vaiṣṇavo viṣṇur evāhaṃ taddāso veti carcayan // [AgMsv_2.316]

plain_english: If one now says, 'I am not thus,' is that really coherent? For in that case, one of the two awarenesses ends up being false knowledge.
sanskrit_cite:
idānīṃ na tathāsmīti kim etat susamañjasam /
atra hy ekatamā saṃvin mithyājñānatvam aśnute // [AgMsv_2.317]

plain_english: By that same outlook a disciple may become fallen, so the main rule is that for each scripture the proper teacher is its own teacher.
sanskrit_cite:
yayā sa eva patitaḥ śiṣyo vā patito bhavet /
tasmān mukhyo hy ayaṃ kalpaḥ pratiśāstraṃ gurur guruḥ // [AgMsv_2.318]

plain_english: The independent scriptures say that someone devoted to another scripture, or even absorbed in that other scripture, does not give the fruit of spiritual attainment.
sanskrit_cite:
uktaṃ svatantraśāstreṣu nāsau siddhiphalapradaḥ /
anyaśāstrarato yaḥ syāt tacchāstranirato 'pi vā // [AgMsv_2.319]

plain_english: Even in ordinary life the same convention holds: Vishnu is served by Bhagavatas, the Sun by Magas, Shambhu by ash-smeared ascetics, the Mothers by their specialists, Brahma by brahmins, the Buddha by Shakyas, and the Arhat by naked ascetics; whoever worships a deity by its own method should perform that deity's rite.
sanskrit_cite:
loke 'pi yāvad īdṛkṣaḥ pravādo jyotirādike /

viṣṇor bhāgavatā magāś ca savituḥ śāṃbhor jaṭābhasmino māt-ṛṇām atha mātṛmaṇḍalavido viprās tv atha brahmaṇaḥ /
śākyāḥ sattvahitasya buddhavapuṣo nagnās tathaivārhato yo yair deva upāsyate svavidhinā tais tasya kāryā kriyā // [AgMsv_2.320]

plain_english: Therefore, even if someone with higher knowledge is present in the same place, that does not create different eligibilities.
sanskrit_cite:
ata evādhikajñānaśālī saṃnihito yadi /
deśe tatra bhaven nānā nādhikārasya bhājanam // [AgMsv_2.321]

plain_english: But one who is firmly established in this full awakening and in the real teaching sets the disciple's mind toward ever higher ascent.
sanskrit_cite:
yas tv asmin pūrṇasaṃbodhe rūḍho vāstavaśāsane /
uttarottararūḍhyarthaṃ śiśoḥ karaṇamānasam (?) // [AgMsv_2.322]

plain_english: For the attainment of fruit, or for a disciple governed only by a partial disposition, that teacher should indeed bestow grace, because of his fullness and his functioning from a higher level.
sanskrit_cite:
phalasaṃpattaye vāpi bhāvāṃśavaśaśālinaḥ /
anugrahaṃ sa vai kuryāt pūrṇatvād ūrdhvavṛttitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.323]

plain_english: Someone may object: in nonduality, what could be higher? Nothing. The answer is that those who think this are deluded by difference; for you the lower state is difference, because difference itself is lower.
sanskrit_cite:
nanv advaye kim ūrdhvaṃ syān na kiṃcid bhedamohitāḥ /
bhavatas tv adharāvasthā bheda evadharo yataḥ // [AgMsv_2.324]

plain_english: Therefore, any others who follow teachings meant for bound souls—such as Vaishnavas, Buddhists, Vedic ritualists, and Vedanta speakers—are included in that class.
sanskrit_cite:
tasmād ye kecanānye syuḥ paśuśāsanavartinaḥ /
vaiṣṇavāḥ saugatāḥ śrautās tathā śrutyantavādinaḥ // [AgMsv_2.325]

plain_english: Such groups are never authorized in the Lord's teaching, as has been stated in the scriptures when determining who is eligible.
sanskrit_cite:
ityādayo nādhikṛtā jātucit patiśāsane /
uktavān yatra śāstreṣv apy adhikārivivecane // [AgMsv_2.326]

plain_english: If a deluded Vaishnava were to give initiation to a Shaiva disciple, the disciple should abandon that sinful deceiver and follow the proper course.
sanskrit_cite:
yo vaiṣṇavo manuṃ dadyāc chaivaṃ mūḍhamatiḥ śiśoḥ /
taṃ pāpaṃ vañcakaṃ tyaktvā śiśur nyāyyaṃ samācaret // [AgMsv_2.327]

plain_english: Here too it is said that one who gives liberation must possess well-practiced knowledge; and that supreme knowledge is well practiced because there is no falling away from it.
sanskrit_cite:
ihāpy uktaṃ mokṣadaḥ syāt svabhyastajñānavān iti /
abhyastaṃ ca paraṃ jñānaṃ yato nāsty eva vicyutiḥ // [AgMsv_2.328]

plain_english: From supreme nondual realization there is indeed no falling away at all, because its functioning is fully pervaded by all knowledge established on the side of the Self.
sanskrit_cite:
paramādvayavijñānān na khalv apy asti vicyutiḥ /
svātmapakṣasthitāśeṣajñānanirbharavṛttikaḥ // [AgMsv_2.329]

plain_english: How, or who, or from where could it fall away, or where could it stand otherwise? This meaning of the scripture stands firm just as it is, by the power of śakti.
sanskrit_cite:
kathaṃ ko vā kuto vāpi cyavatāṃ tiṣṭhatu kva vā /
itthaṃ ya eṣa śāstrārthaḥ sthitaḥ śaktiprabhāvataḥ // [AgMsv_2.330]

plain_english: Filled within with all principles, letters, and the rest, bearing all names, and whose very nature is Bhairava, he alone abides in his own true form.
sanskrit_cite:
antaḥkṛtāśeṣatattvavarṇādibharanirbharaḥ /
sarvābhidho bhairavātmā so 'yam eva svarūpabhāk // [AgMsv_2.331]

plain_english: In this scripture composed by the Supreme Lord under the name Jñānacandra, I have explained this clear yet profound statement, following the method of establishing the authority of our own tradition and also through various relevant contexts. For those whose minds have entered into it, the greatness of its authority, exalted by universal nonduality, shines forth; sincere-hearted people will know this for themselves, so what need is there for praise?
sanskrit_cite:
śāstre 'smin parameśena jñānacandrākhyayā kṛtaḥ /

tadvyākhyātam idaṃ prasannagahanaṃ vākyaṃ mayā svāgamaprāmāṇyapratipādanakramavaśāt tattatprasaṅgād api /
atrārūḍhadhiyāṃ pramāṇamahimā viśvādvayoddāmito bhātīti svayam eva satyahṛdayā jñāsyanti kiṃ ślāghitaiḥ // [AgMsv_2.332]

plain_english: Those who inquire properly are truly auspicious, so what effort is needed toward them? And what use is there with those who are lame in climbing the far peak of reflective awareness and whose conduct has turned to stone? As for those people barren of scripture, their vehemence is like the ocean at cosmic dissolution; therefore this agitation only whirls back within oneself.
sanskrit_cite:
ye samyak pravicāriṇo nanu śivāḥ kas tān prati prodyamaḥ kiṃ tair ye pravimarśadūraśikharārohakrame paṅgavaḥ /
pāṣāṇāyitavṛttayaḥ punar amī ye śāstravandhyā narāḥ saṃrambhaḥ pralayambudher iva tataḥ svātmany ayaṃ ghūrṇate // [AgMsv_2.333]

plain_english: Grow calm of yourself within the self; quickly abandon your ostentatious display of flaming matted locks, O fire of cosmic dissolution. There is nothing left for you to burn now, because by hundreds of terrible, dense, whirling sparks of your blazing, this universe has been pervaded and swiftly dissolved, becoming of the nature of your own light.
sanskrit_cite:
saṃśāmya svayam ātmani tyaja javāj jvālājaṭāḍambarān bhoḥ kalpānala dāhyam asti bhavato nādyāpi kiñcid yataḥ /
tvatprollāsavighūrṇanāghanaghuradghorasphuliṅgaśatair viśvaṃ vyāpya vilīnatāṃ gatam idaṃ drāk tvatprakāśātmakam // [AgMsv_2.334]

plain_english: In the eastern city named Pravarapura, the Kashmirian Abhinavagupta composed this vārttika on the great teaching beginning with the Mālinī.
sanskrit_cite:
pravarapuranāmadheye pure pūrve kāśmīriko 'bhinavaguptaḥ /
mālinyādimavākye vārttikam etad racayati sma // [AgMsv_2.335]
